title: Add foreground and scheduled drift review reminders

requirement.summary: Add one shared, repo-native cadence contract that reminds users to review requirement, architecture, and functionality drift in active AgentGov sessions and opt-in scheduled CI.

objective.rationale: The human product owner selected the combined foreground-plus-CI direction after reviewing the reminder, authority, and hidden-daemon trade-offs.

goal: Implement a lightweight drift-review cadence that becomes due after three completed tasks or seven days, appears non-blockingly in the foreground and Monitor, and can be surfaced by future-version scheduled CI without presenting advisory judgment as a failing check.
non_goals: Do not create a hidden daemon, desktop service, SaaS control plane, central telemetry, or automatic local-state upload.
Do not objectively decide requirement, architecture, or functionality correctness; semantic drift conclusions remain advisory and human-owned.
Do not automatically edit requirements, ADRs, task scope, policy, application code, or governance decisions.
Do not create GitHub issues, send email or chat messages, or add any external notification write authority.
Do not change the published 0.2.1 or v0.3.0rc1 release identity or claim that an unreleased development-source command exists in those wheels.
Do not commit, push, publish, release, deploy, merge, or activate a workflow in a consumer repository.
acceptance_signals: One strict repository policy and immutable review-record contract drive both foreground and CI due-state calculation with default thresholds of three completed tasks or seven days.
Due-state calculation is deterministic, while requirement, architecture, and functionality conclusions are explicitly advisory and never reported as objective failures.
An active foreground cycle surfaces one non-blocking reminder without displacing task, scope, or completion decisions; acknowledged review or seven-day snooze resets the appropriate cadence boundary.
The Development Monitor displays the current drift-review state, reasons, evidence limits, and denied authority without claiming that the user read or resolved the reminder.

A future-version managed GitHub Actions workflow can run the same read-only status command on schedule, write a warning and job summary while remaining green, and grants no issue, email, chat, merge, release, or deployment authority.
The published 0.2.1 and v0.3.0rc1 workflow renderings remain byte-compatible with their existing command surface.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_drift_review tests.test_foreground_coordinator tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_development_monitor tests.test_consumer_ci -v
python -m unittest tests.test_initializer tests.test_templates tests.test_public_documentation_freshness tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A periodic semantic opinion could be mislabeled as a deterministic failure.
Foreground reminders could displace a higher-priority authority decision or create notification fatigue.
A scheduled workflow could imply external notification authority or break a pinned published release.
Mutable or unbounded review state could weaken repository history and privacy boundaries.

stop_conditions: Stop before any hidden daemon, external notification write, telemetry upload, automatic semantic verdict, automatic governance-file mutation, or blocking advisory result.
Stop if the foreground reminder cannot remain subordinate to task, scope, completion, and consequential authority decisions.
Stop if scheduled CI requires changing an already-published workflow contract or marking an advisory reminder as a deterministic failure.
Stop before any commit, push, publication, release, deployment, merge, or consumer workflow activation.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-09, the product owner selected the combined foreground-session and scheduled-CI reminder direction after reviewing the three alternatives. The bounded slice is implemented and validated: semantic drift remains advisory, scheduled notification is read-only and non-failing, foreground reminders remain subordinate to higher-priority governance cards, and hidden daemons and external notification writes remain excluded. The task is paused for product-owner review; no follow-on requirement, Git action, publication, release, deployment, or workflow activation is authorized.
